concerns.text: Task T023 implements a 'random-pattern' control arm, creating a three-group design. This directly contradicts Spec FR-003 and US-2 which mandate exactly two groups (pattern-guided vs. baseline) for 50 pairs. This is a semantic weakening of the experimental design constraint.

Task T008a specifies a fallback to `all-mpnet-base-v2` if memory constraints are hit. This model is larger than the primary `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` and will violate the 7 GB RAM constraint (Spec US-1, Plan Constraints). The fallback logic itself violates the memory constraint it aims to solve.

Task T031 requires implementing a 'recruitment pipeline' to verify ORCIDs and collect ratings on a GitHub Actions runner. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Plan constraints, as an isolated CI runner cannot automate the recruitment of real human experts. The task scope is infeasible and contradicts the 'blind evaluation' requirement which implies external human input.

Task T036 implements outlier removal via IQR filtering on raw rows. This risks breaking the paired structure required for the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (FR-005) if pairs are unbalanced after filtering. The spec requires sensitivity analysis but does not authorize breaking the pairing invariant.

Tasks T027 and T037 focus on correlating retrieval thresholds with scores. SC-004 explicitly states validity is measured by 'downstream expert scores' ensuring statistical significance, not the retrieval mechanism's predictive power. These tasks measure the wrong variable defined in the success criterion.
